instructions: Put the brisket in a large pot with the onion cut in half, 4 of the garlic cloves smashed with the side of your knife, the daikon cut into large chunks, and 9 cups of water. Bring it to a boil over high heat and skim off the foam.
Turn the heat to medium-low, partly cover and simmer for 1 hour, until a fork slides into the brisket easily.
Meanwhile, cut the green onions into 3-inch lengths. Tear the mushrooms into bite-size pieces and rinse the bean sprouts. Mince the remaining 2 garlic cloves.

Make the chili oil for the table. Heat the neutral oil and sesame oil in a small pan over low heat for 30 seconds. Add the gochugaru and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty. Don't let it brown. Transfer it to a small bowl.

Bring a medium pot of water to a boil. Add the bean sprouts and boil for 10 seconds. Add the mushrooms and green onions and boil for 10 seconds. Drain, rinse under cold water, and gently squeeze out the extra water.

Transfer the brisket to a cutting board. Strain the broth into a clean pot and throw away the onion, garlic and daikon. That should be about 7 cups of broth. Let the brisket cool for 10 minutes, then shred it along the grain with your fingers.
Toss the shredded beef with the minced garlic, gochujang, 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and the pepper.
Add the beef and the vegetables to the broth. Bring it to a simmer, then cover and cook over medium-low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir in the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce. Taste it. If it's flat, add the salt a pinch at a time.
Ladle the soup into bowls and serve with the chili oil on the side for the adults.

To keep leftovers, let the soup cool, then store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week or in the freezer for up to 3 months. Reheat over medium heat until it's steaming, without a hard boil.
method_notes: Beyond Kimchee simmers brisket with onion, garlic and radish, shreds it, and finishes a big pot with blanched sprouts, mushrooms and leeks in a chili oil and soup soy sauce. Korean Bapsang makes a simpler pot of brisket, green onions and sprouts seasoned by hand. Neither has 20 ratings, so the lead is a fallback. This one follows Beyond Kimchee, scaled to 1 lb of brisket, with regular soy sauce in place of soup soy sauce, no dried fernbrake or anchovy sauce, and the chili oil served at the table so the pot stays mild.
